title: Redington Ltd - 532805 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Redington Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR43,002 crores and PAT excluding exceptionals rose 50% to INR581 crores, with Arena still loss-making.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and PAT, with growth broad across India, GCC, Africa and the UAE, led by TSG (up 91%) on AI server and GPU migration. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue reached INR77,967 crores (up 41%) and PAT excluding exceptionals INR1,067 crores (up 61%). Arena remained the drag: revenue fell 37% YoY and Redington's share of loss was INR115 crores, including transition and impairment charges. Management flagged elevated receivable provisions, inventory above comfortable levels, rising debt, and possible softening in consumer demand after price increases.

segments.name: India distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution business grew 67% YoY in the quarter, the fastest of the regions cited.

segments.name: Rest of World ex-Arena
segments.commentary: Grew 38% YoY; GCC and Levant ex-UAE/KSA +121%, UAE +39%, Africa +35%, Middle East overall +41%.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY and was 34% of consolidated revenue; SISA geography grew 70%; Rest of World Mobility grew 34% ex-Arena.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 38% YoY to 30% of revenue, driven mainly by higher ASPs plus a sequential rise in commercial PC volumes; highest quarterly revenue to date.

segments.name: Technology Solutions Group (TSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 91% YoY to 20% of mix; large deals above INR3,800 crores (about 9% of group revenue), mostly data centres and neo-cloud. Ex-large deals TSG grew about 33-35%.

segments.name: Software Solutions Group (SSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 39% YoY to 15% of revenue, with all SBUs growing, led by cybersecurity and cloud; SSG gross margin above 6%.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 37% YoY; exited the VDF contract and high-interest Lira working capital business; new management in place; Q2 loss includes transition provisions and impairment.

guidance_outlook: Management sees H2 FY27 growth north of 25% at overall business level, with caveats on price-driven demand contraction and West Asia impact on UAE, KSA and GCC.
H2 seasonality is expected to be muted this year because price increases and shortages pulled consumption forward; H2 is normally bigger than H1.
Sustainable quarterly opex guided at INR950-1,000 crores.
TSG expected to be the strongest growth driver in H2, followed by SSG; ESG and MSG approached with more caution due to price-volume elasticity.
Neo-cloud opportunity in India estimated at INR150,000 crores over the next four years; data centre margins below the 4.5-5% run-rate, with ROCE targets maintained.
Management expects SSG and TSG gross margin to improve over 3-5 years through orchestration and services; debt-equity may rise, with equity raise possible if growth needs it.
capex_capacity: Funded capital investment for the data centre large deals is almost nil; only non-funded (bank guarantee) capacity is used, per the CFO India.
Funding strategy: additional debt is currently sufficient; dividend moderation or equity raise are options if the growth trend requires it.
Debt-equity is about 0.5-0.6x; management cited global distribution peers at 0.6-0.8x and said distribution is working-capital intensive, typically above 1:1.
Five AI learning centres rolled out in India over the last two quarters (CSR); AI COE launched in Singapore with a physical experience centre and a virtual COE in build.
demand_pricing: Smartphone and PC prices up roughly 30-50% YoY; enterprise AI PC adoption above 40% in commercial, consumer around 10%.
Consumer PC/smartphone units declining; Microsoft activation data down 20-30% for consumer, while commercial PC activation is 0-7% growth.
Enterprise is about two-thirds of Redington's PC business and consumer about one-third; Mobility is roughly equal consumer-type, so IT is about half-half.
Management views market share as flat to a slight gain, with no loss.
Channel inventory above comfortable levels as partners hold stock ahead of price increases; Middle East supply chains stressed (Strait of Hormuz closed, alternate routes adding turnaround time).
Gross margin ex-large deals about 5.13%; reported gross margin broadly similar QoQ.
AI exchange platform in early traction, engaging hundreds of partners; described as a long-term journey.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins trending down despite lower Mobility mix, and how sustainable is the TSG large-deal pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TSG jump is a CPU-to-GPU migration with roughly 4x ASPs, not just pricing, and expects it to continue. CFO said margins ex-large deals were 5.13%, similar to last year, and that Arena's higher-margin local-currency business in prior-year quarters affects comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Arena losses rise to about INR70 crores in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were three components: business loss, Lira transition provisions (rebates and discounts not aligned with vendor support), and a INR40 crore intangibles impairment. Business loss alone was much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable opex and what provisions were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex was elevated by receivable provisions, SSG investments, and Middle East war-related insurance costs. Sustainable run-rate is INR950-1,000 crores per quarter. Receivable provisions were about INR213 crores (INR67 crores SISA, INR135 crores Arena); inventory provisioning was not material.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth be funded and what are the levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is sufficient for now; levers include more debt, moderating dividends, or raising equity, which will be used if the growth trend requires it. Debt-equity of 0.5-0.6x was described as comfortable versus 0.6-0.8x for global peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth exceed 25%, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no reason to pull back from north of 25% H2 growth, with caveats on price-led demand contraction and West Asia impact. Seasonality is expected to be muted because price increases pulled demand forward.

qa_highlights.question: Would a slowdown in AI capex affect the FY29/FY30 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TSG and data-centre business would be affected by any AI capex pullback; SSG (cloud, security) and smartphones less so. PCs could see some impact, but the market is expected to rationalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the neo-cloud opportunity and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: India neo-cloud capacity is expected to go from 1.5 GW to 7 GW and then 12 GW; INR150,000 crore opportunity over four years. Margins are below the 4.5-5% run rate, but ROCE targets are maintained with less incremental opex.

qa_highlights.question: When will Arena turn around?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Arena has exited high-interest Lira working capital business and is near the end of that transition, but partner health and Turkish market issues make a turnaround timeline hard to estimate.

risks_watch: Arena (Turkey) receivables and liquidity, plus a new management team and further restructuring; Q2 loss of INR115 crores including INR40 crore impairment.
Price-led demand elasticity in consumer PCs and smartphones after 30-50% price increases; possible post-Diwali demand contraction.
Channel inventory above comfortable levels, with working-capital build and Q2 FCF of negative INR1,871 crores.
West Asia conflict impact on UAE, KSA and GCC, including logistics, collection cycles and insurance costs.
TSG large deals are lumpy in data centres; AI capex pullback risk for TSG and FY29/FY30 targets.
Rising debt and possible equity raise or dividend moderation as working capital grows.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and TSG momentum, but cautious on consumer demand, Arena, Middle East disruption and channel inventory. Management repeatedly flagged unknowns and declined to estimate Arena's turnaround timing. The CEO took the call from hospital, which the CFO noted, so answers were brief.

financial_highlights.change: Lower end of 35-40 day guidance range
H1 FY27 positive INR583 crores (as cited in Q&A)
Includes ~INR67 crores SISA and ~INR135 crores Arena
Includes INR40 crores impairment of intangibles
Broadly flat QoQ; similar to last year

key_quotes: We delivered the strongest quarterly revenue and profit after tax in our history, not in the benign environment, but against a backdrop of geopolitical disruption, changing component prices and continued supply chain complexity.
It's not really a pricing phenomenon as a lot of people think. There is a real transition happening from CPUs to GPUs.
Arena has exited from the high interest rate working capital business and we believe we are towards the end of that piece.
Normally, H2 has always been better than H1.
So, at this point in time, we are able to manage with the debt. And the other levers, we will bring in when there is a requirement.

adds.what: Five AI learning centres rolled out in India (CSR, not revenue-generating capacity)
AI COE in Singapore with physical experience centre; virtual COE in build

growth.why: Management affirmed H2 FY27 revenue growth north of 25% (guidance new this call), backed partly by TSG neo-cloud and data centre large deals (~9% of revenue), SSG and Rest of World momentum, but with no specific capacity additions and caveats on consumer price-driven demand contraction and muted H2 seasonality.

mgmt.note: New management in place at Arena (Turkey) after exiting the VDF contract and high-interest Lira working capital business; no specific growth plan stated for Arena beyond transition.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin ex-large deals about 5.13%, broadly flat QoQ and similar to last year; Arena losses (INR115 crores incl. INR40 crore impairment) and INR213 crores receivable provisions weigh on margins, and data centre margins are below the 4.5-5% run-rate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical plant or fleet capacity addition discussed; only five AI learning centres (CSR, not revenue-generating) already rolled out and an AI COE in Singapore under construction.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 revenue growth north of 25%, backed by TSG neo-cloud and data centre large deals (~9% of group revenue) and SSG/Rest of World momentum, though consumer PC and smartphone units are declining after 30-50% price increases.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Funded capex for data centre deals is almost nil and only non-funded bank guarantee capacity is used; neo-cloud India capacity is expected to go from 1.5 GW to 7 GW to 12 GW, but no capex plan or amount was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management affirmed H2 FY27 growth north of 25% but flagged consumer price-led demand contraction, muted seasonality and West Asia disruption, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Caveats on price-driven consumer demand, possible post-Diwali contraction, channel inventory above comfortable levels and West Asia impact on UAE, KSA and GCC could pressure the >25% H2 growth guide; Q2 FCF was negative INR1,871 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI exchange platform is in early traction with hundreds of partners and the AI COE in Singapore is under construction, but no commercial product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Arena turnaround timing
rows.why: Arena revenue fell 37% YoY and Q2 loss was INR115 crores; management exited the Lira working capital business and declined to estimate turnaround timing given partner health and Turkish market issues.

rows.label: Debt and equity funding need
rows.why: Debt-equity is about 0.5-0.6x and rising debt is flagged; management said debt is sufficient for now but dividend moderation or an equity raise are options if growth requires it.

rows.label: Inventory and working capital build
rows.why: Channel inventory is above comfortable levels with Q2 FCF at negative INR1,871 crores, though working capital days were at 35, the low end of the 35-40 day guide, and H1 FCF was positive INR583 crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on TSG momentum, AI server migration and the H2 growth guide above 25%, but cautious on consumer demand elasticity, Arena, Middle East disruption and channel inventory; analysts pressed on margins, Arena losses, and funding, and the CEO's brief answers from hospital limited
